newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, seen consolidating.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.25 percent on Thursday on low turnover and traders expect the market to consolidate over the short-term.
"Today, shares rose in reaction to recent low levels, next week prices could rise a bit, but there will be no major move until foreigners return to buying," Andrej Obed, a trader at A bank said.

The Bank of Slovenia a month ago blocked the inflow of foreign investments by ordering international portfolio investors to open custodian accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to trade in Slovenian shares.
Banks said costs for opening accounts would be about 12 percent of the amount handled.

"Even if costs would not be too high for international investors they could easily pull out of Slovenian market and go to some other investor-friendlier market in the region," a trader at a foreign bank in Slovenia said.
The SBI index rose 3.42 points to 1,396.34. In five consecutive days of gains the index has risen just 2.1 percent.
Overall seven shares rose, five fell and four were unchanged, while 10 were untraded. Turnover fell to 54.1 million tolars from 55.9 million.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active, easing 0.07 percent to 27,040 tolars on volume of 507 shares for total turnover of 13.7 million tolars.
Brokerage Primofin was the biggest gainer, firming 3.16 percent to 13,400 tolars on volume of 186 shares.
Ordinary shares of trading company Kovinotehna led the day's decliners, falling 7.55 percent to 490 tolars on volume of 983 shares.
